item.title: Enhanced Stabilization of Steel Slag for Road Aggregate via Dual-Functional-Group Chelation of Poly(acrylic acid- co -vinylphosphonic acid)
item.description:
Abstract
The volume expansion induced by residual free calcium oxide (f-CaO) in steel slag remains the primary limitation to its widespread application in pavement engineering. To address this issue, a novel polymer modifier (PAV) was synthesized via the aqueous radical polymerization of acrylic acid (AA) and vinylphosphonic acid (VPA). The effects of monomer ratios on the chemical structure, thermal stability, and Ca2+ chelation performance of PAV were systematically investigated using GPC, FTIR, SEM-EDS, and TGA. The modification mechanism of PAV on steel slag was revealed through systematic characterization and performance tests. Furthermore, the key process parameters for PAV-modified steel slag were optimized, and the volume stability and mechanical properties of the modified steel slag were comprehensively evaluated. The results indicated that the synthesized PAV exhibited a uniform molecular weight distribution and excellent thermal stability. Through the chelation effect of carboxyl and phosphonic acid groups, PAV can efficiently eliminate f-CaO in steel slag. When the mass ratio of AA to VPA is 8.5:1.5, PAV exhibits the optimal Ca2+ chelation performance, with a chelation capacity reaching 376 mg/g. The optimal modification concentration of PAV was determined to be 1.0 wt %. Under this condition, the f-CaO content of the modified steel slag was reduced to 0.54%, with a 10-day water immersion expansion rate of merely 0.46%, which was far below the standard limit. Meanwhile, the PAV modification did not damage the inorganic crystalline skeleton of the steel slag. Instead, it reduced its water absorption, aggregate crushing value, and Los Angeles abrasion value, thereby further optimizing its mechanical properties.

item.title: Study on Ionic Liquid-Modified ZIF-8 Composite Materials and Their CO 2 Adsorption Performance
item.description:
Abstract
Driven by the dual carbon goals, developing novel carbon capture technologies is crucial. Adsorption methods have become a research focus due to their simplicity in operation, wide range of adsorbent options, and low cost. To enhance the CO2 adsorption performance of ZIF-8, this study employed amino acid–based ionic liquids as modifiers ([emim]Gly and N2222Gly) to prepare ZIF-IL composite materials via the impregnation method. The structural characteristics of the composite materials were characterized, and their CO2 adsorption performances were evaluated. Results indicated that the ILs were successfully loaded onto the pores and surface of ZIF-8 through hydrogen bonding and coordination interactions. ZIF-[emim]Gly and ZIF-N2222Gly retained intact crystalline structures and polyhedral morphologies, but the specific surface area and pore volume decreased, indicating that the incorporation of ILs occupied part of the pores of ZIF-8. CO2 adsorption tests revealed that the adsorption capacities of ZIF-8, ZIF-[emim]Gly, and ZIF-N2222Gly were 1.27, 0.83, and 0.74 mmol·g–1, respectively, under the conditions of 700 mmHg and 298 K. Although ZIF-[emim]Gly and ZIF-8-N2222Gly provided additional active sites for CO2 adsorption via acid–base synergistic effects, they could not compensate for the loss of pore structure of ZIF-8. However, compared with ZIF-8, the CO2/N2 selectivity of ZIF-[emim]Gly and ZIF-N2222Gly was significantly improved. The isosteric heats of ZIF-8, ZIF-[emim]Gly, and ZIF-8-N2222Gly were 8.3–11.7, 10.7–36.7, and 9.1–25.7 kJ·mol–1, respectively. The introduction of ILs significantly enhanced the adsorption forces for CO2, providing experimental and theoretical foundations for the development of high-performance CO2 adsorption materials.

item.title: Synthesis and SERS Evaluation of Cu/Cu 2 O Microtubes
item.description:
Abstract
In this work, Cu/Cu2O microtubes were fabricated by electroless deposition on polymer templates and evaluated as substrates for surface-enhanced Raman spectroscopy (SERS). The structural, morphological, and optical properties of the substrate were characterized by XRD, SEM/EDS, XPS, and UV–vis spectroscopy. XRD analysis confirmed the formation of face-centered cubic copper (90.1%) with a minor Cu2O phase (9.9%), while XPS showed that the surface was dominated by Cu0/Cu+ species with a minor contribution from Cu2+ species. UV–vis absorption spectroscopy revealed a broad absorption band in the 400–600 nm range. Additional electromagnetic modeling was used to evaluate the optical and near-field response of the Cu structures. The SERS performance of the substrate was evaluated using four probe analytes: methylene blue, methyl violet, eosin yellow, and potassium chromate. Analytical enhancement factors ranging from 0.2 × 103 to 0.8 × 104 were obtained, depending on the analyte.

item.title: Ligand-Free Ni 2+ Immobilization on Poly(acrylic acid)-Functionalized Magnetic Nanoparticles for His-Tagged Protein Purification
item.description:
Abstract
The development of simplified, ligand-free magnetic affinity platforms holds promise for advancing future recombinant protein purification technologies. Purification of His6-tagged proteins, essential in biotechnology and biopharmaceutical production, is commonly achieved via immobilized metal ion affinity chromatography (IMAC). However, magnetic IMAC systems commonly require additional chelating ligands for Ni2+ immobilization, increasing surface functionalization complexity. Developing a ligand-free magnetic platform for direct Ni2+ immobilization could therefore simplify this purification process. Poly(acrylic acid) (PAA)-functionalized magnetic nanoparticles (MNPs) were developed as a simple ligand-free platform for direct Ni2+ immobilization and selective purification of His6-tagged proteins, exploiting the intrinsic metal-coordination capability of surface carboxylate groups. MNPs were synthesized by chemical coprecipitation and subsequently coated with PAA of two molecular weights (2 and 100 kDa) to systematically investigate the influence of polymer chain length on physicochemical properties, Ni2+ immobilization efficiency, and bioseparation performance. ATR-FTIR spectroscopy revealed a decrease in the free carboxylic acid stretching band and a concurrent increase in the carboxylate coordination band upon Ni2+ immobilization, supporting the involvement of PAA carboxylate groups in Ni2+ immobilization, consistent with a proposed carboxylate–metal interaction at the nanoparticle surface. Complementarily, zeta potential analysis demonstrated progressive surface charge evolution from bare MNPs to PAA-coated and Ni2+-loaded states, consistent with PAA adsorption and subsequent Ni2+ immobilization. The purification performance of both systems was then evaluated using His6-tagged Plasmodium falciparum serine hydroxymethyltransferase (His6-tagged PfSHMT) as a model protein. Despite both systems achieving near-complete adsorption, MNPs–PAA(2 kDa)–Ni2+ exhibited significantly higher desorption efficiency (63.5 ± 6.7%) than MNPs–PAA(100 kDa)–Ni2+ (37.8 ± 6.1%), demonstrating different protein recovery between the two PAA formulations investigated. The optimized MNPs–PAA(2 kDa)–Ni2+ system achieved rapid protein capture within 15 min and selective purification over nontagged proteins (BSA and lysozyme). Further application to crude E. coli cell lysate demonstrated enrichment of His6-tagged PfSHMT with retained enzymatic activity and a 326-fold purification. These findings establish PAA-functionalized MNPs as a simple and effective ligand-free nanoplatform for selective affinity-based bioseparation of His6-tagged proteins.

item.title: Flexible Solar-Blind Ultraviolet Photodetector Based on a Freestanding β-Ga 2 O 3 /BTO Semiconductor/Ferroelectric Heterostructure
item.description:
Abstract
Excessive ultraviolet (UV) exposure causes cumulative harm to human health, creating a growing demand for wearable devices that enable real-time UV monitoring. Among various UV-sensitive materials, β-Ga2O3 is particularly attractive because of its wide bandgap, intrinsic solar-blind response, high sensitivity, and excellent stability. However, its intrinsic brittleness and the high temperatures required for growth on rigid substrates limit its use in flexible electronics. Here, we report a flexible solar-blind Ga2O3 photodetector based on a freestanding ferroelectric BaTiO3 (BTO)/Ga2O3 heterostructure fabricated using a nondestructive, water-soluble transfer strategy. Spontaneous polarization in the BTO layer generates a built-in electric field that promotes the separation of photogenerated carriers. In addition, polarization rotation and domain evolution provide ferroelastic strain accommodation, enabling effective stress relaxation and improving the mechanical stability of the flexible device. The device retained more than 90% of its initial photocurrent after 1000 bending cycles at a bending radius of 7.5 mm. It was further integrated into wearable devices, including a wristband, smart sunglasses, and a ring, demonstrating its mechanical conformability and integration capability on wearable platforms. This work offers an effective strategy for integrating brittle wide-bandgap semiconductors into flexible devices and advances wearable solar-blind UV sensing technologies.

item.title: Dual-Functional Halloysite Nanotube-Derived Cigarette Capsules for Hazard Reduction and Mold Prevention
item.description:
Abstract
Currently, cigarette-filter modification has predominantly targeted reactive oxygen species (ROS) scavenging; however, beyond ROS, cigarette smoke contains other hazardous agents such as carbon monoxide (CO), tar, and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the reduction of which remains largely neglected in current strategies. Herein, we report a novel cigarette-filter capsule, termed Cit-sHNT@Capsule, fabricated by loading the natural flavor citral (Cit) into sulfuric acid-etched halloysite nanotubes and further encapsulating the hybrid within alginate-based hydrogel beads. Incorporating Cit-sHNT@Capsule into cigarette filters moderately reduced CO and tar yields by 9.74% and 13.4%, respectively, while the •OH and •O2– probe assays indicated reductions of approximately 50% and 60%, and fluorescence-based calibration yielded an apparent 57.0% reduction in the PAH-associated measurement, without compromising the moisture and nicotine content during combustion. Thermogravimetric analysis indicated limited mass loss over 70–80 °C, and the capsules retained their structural integrity under the heating conditions, providing preliminary support for their incorporation into cigarette filters. Furthermore, the outstanding antifungal activity of Cit-sHNT@Capsule against Aspergillus niger (nearly 100% inhibition within 45 days) underscored the potential to extend tobacco storage duration and reduce fungal contamination. Collectively, this work highlights the potential of Cit-sHNT@Capsule as a dual-functional additive for cigarette filters, enabling simultaneous hazard reduction and mold prevention.

item.title: Influence of a Single Nitrogen Atom on the π–π Stacking Interaction in Coronene Dimers: An EDA, QTAIM, and NCI Computational Analysis
item.description:
Abstract
Intermolecular aromatic interactions, also known as π–π stacking, are of great importance in chemical and biological materials science. This field of study has remained important for at least three decades and spans a broad multidisciplinary range. Doping aromatic systems with heteroatoms, such as nitrogen, can influence these interactions and significantly alter their properties. Still, the exact cause of the altered π–π interactions in aromatic aggregates from heteroatom doping remains debated. In this work, we evaluate changes in the electronic and structural properties of coronene dimers upon introducing a single nitrogen heteroatom. Calculations use CAM–B3LYP–D3/6–311G(d,p) level of theory, along with EDA, QTAIM, and NCI analyses. Our results show that nitrogen subtly enhances π–π interactions between coronene monomers. The strength of these interactions varies with the substitution site. Aggregation becomes stronger with increased N–N distance when pyridinic–N is the substituent, if the same arrangement is considered (twisted or parallel–displaced). When graphitic–N is substituted at an intermediary position, the degree of slipping between monomers mainly governs aggregation, regardless of the arrangement. In the central ring, graphitic–N promotes the formation of a covalent C–C bond between the monomers, promoting a 10 kcal mol–1 increase in interaction energy. The results indicate that dispersive forces, such as pancake bond, remain the primary driver of aggregation, with nitrogen only slightly altering the electronic charge distribution. Energy decomposition analysis indicates that dispersion remains the dominant stabilizing contribution, while the type and position of the nitrogen atom locally modulate the electronic environment and promote distinct geometrical reorganizations of the π–π interface, thereby affecting the interaction strength and preferred stacking arrangements.

item.title: Scientific Insights into the Illegible and Discolored Red and Green Inks in Arabic Papyrus Protocols
item.description:
Abstract
Papyrus protocols are texts written on the outermost sheet of a papyrus roll, providing information relevant to its manufacture in a state-controlled facility. Arabic papyrus protocols constitute a key corpus of manuscripts that feature colored inks in early Islamic Egypt, with red and green inks used alongside iron-gall ink for writing the text. To expand our limited knowledge of the early Islamic color palette, 14 Arabic papyrus protocols preserved at the Austrian National Library in Vienna were subjected to non-destructive analysis combining scanning XRF spectroscopy with vibrational spectroscopies. Visual examination indicated that both colored inks exhibited signs of degradation. The red ink, in particular, appeared to be significantly discolored, rendering sections of the text illegible. The green ink was identified as a copper-based green, with moolooite (CuC2O4·nH2O) as the primary component. The red ink was identified as red lead (Pb3O4). Chlorine was also detected alongside lead in the red ink in 12 cases; its presence could be attributed to both intrinsic (e.g., ink formulation) and extrinsic (e.g., migration from a chlorine-rich environment) factors. The results from semi-quantitative analysis suggested that the Pb3O4 content in the red ink, though low, was sufficient to create a clear contrast on a fresh papyrus sheet. Based on these results, we tentatively propose that the observed discoloration was likely caused by a combination of factors, including pigment and support degradation. Finally, the results allowed us to improve the legibility of the faded sections of the text and reconstruct their original layout.

item.title: Thermally Altered Pore-Fracture Structures and Water Seepage Behaviors in Shale Characterized by LF-NMR Measurements and Numerical Simulations
item.description:
Abstract
Shale is a tight medium with low porosity and permeability, and fluid seepage takes place across interconnected pores and fractures. Thermal stimulation triggers shale cracking, alters pore-fracture geometry, fluid properties, and seepage rules, so as to boost shale gas output. Most existing studies on shale fluid flow under temperature conditions focus solely on either freeze damage at low temperatures or thermal damage at high temperatures. They lack comprehensive characterization over a wide temperature range spanning from extremely low to moderate-to-high temperatures. Furthermore, most studies regard experimental testing and numerical simulation as separate efforts. Few investigations combine low-field nuclear magnetic resonance (LF-NMR) microporosity measurements and scanning electron microscopy (SEM)-reconstructed thermo-hydro-mechanical (THM) multiphysics simulations for comparative validation. Studying fluid flow in shale pore-fracture networks under variable temperatures is practically important for efficient shale gas exploitation. In this work, shale outcrops from Jiujiang were tested via LF-NMR and COMSOL THM simulations to clarify pore-fracture evolution, fluid distribution, and water seepage features under different thermal conditions. T2 spectra show low-temperature freezing forms ice plugs inside pores, cutting pore connectivity, and movable fluid volume. High temperatures weaken mineral adsorption to release bound water; thermal expansion and cracking connect tiny pores to form unobstructed flow channels. Real pore-fracture models reconstructed from SEM images were adopted for coupled simulations. Simulation outcomes indicate that frost heave squeezes pore throats at low temperatures, raising flow resistance and lowering permeability. Rising temperature reduces water viscosity and generates thermal fractures, greatly improving seepage capacity. Consistent trends between tests and simulations verify the model reliability. Temperature controls shale seepage via two paths: changing fluid physical properties and reconstructing pore-fracture systems. Ice blockage restrains water migration under cold conditions, whereas fluid activation and thermal fractures enhance seepage at high temperatures. This study offers theoretical support for reservoir stimulation and underground high-temperature formation safety assessment.

item.title: All-Protein Electrospun Scaffolds: Profiling Time-dependent Spinnable Regimes and the Addition of Functional Fillers
item.description:
Abstract
Electrospinning is a well-established and scalable technology, enabling the production of fibrous scaffolds for the healthcare, packaging, and food technology industries. Given the rising global emphasis on sustainable development, there is broad interest in adapting existing processing technologies, such as electrospinning, for the production of fully bio-based and biodegradable material platforms. However, processing of such materials, including globular proteins, without synthetic carrier polymers remains a considerable challenge. Here, we systematically explore solvent-mediated structural changes of bovine serum albumin (BSA) as a model globular protein and map electrospinnable regimes. Time-resolved circular dichroism and rheological analyses reveal partial protein unfolding and significant rheological changes in a time window that corresponds to electrospinnability, yielding scaffolds with uniform ∼1 μm diameter fibers. We also introduce BSA and hen egg white lysozyme (Lys) protein nanofibrils (PNFs) as functional fillers to modify the resulting scaffold properties. PNFs increase the effective Young’s modulus, particularly for hydrazone crosslinkable BSA and Lys, whereby electrospun scaffold morphology is preserved in both dry and hydrated states. Electrospun scaffolds were non-cytotoxic to NIH/3T3 fibroblasts and sustained their proliferation over the course of 5 days, highlighting such materials as sustainable, water-stable scaffolds for potential biomedical applications.

item.title: Stage-Gated Biomaterial Strategies for Peri-Implantitis Management
item.description:
Abstract
Peri-implant biomaterials are commonly compared as isolated antimicrobial technologies, although their clinical relevance depends on linked requirements spanning prevention and treatment. Preventive approaches must preserve tissue integration and future cleanability; once disease develops, treatment must provide access to and disruption of mature biofilm, preserve or recover implant-surface competence, control destructive inflammation, support defect-specific regeneration, and enable durable maintenance. This structured critical review proposes a six-gate framework that evaluates preventive surfaces, decontamination methods, local delivery systems, host-directed materials, and regenerative adjuncts against those downstream requirements. Human peri-implant evidence was prioritized for treatment claims. Animal studies, clinically representative in vitro models, simplified implant models, and indirect oral-biofilm or general materials evidence were considered separately. The synthesis shows that mechanical and surgical strategies have the most direct clinical evidence, but no decontamination protocol has shown consistent, durable superiority across clinical settings. Reconstructive biomaterials can improve radiographic defect fill in selected defects, but their additional benefit for composite disease resolution remains uncertain. Meanwhile, antimicrobial coatings, plasma electrolytic oxidation platforms, smart hydrogels, and immunomodulatory materials remain supported mainly by preclinical models. Across different technologies, the same bottlenecks recur restricted access to threaded and protein-conditioned surfaces, reliance on immature or simplified biofilms, unmeasured surface damage or chemical residues, incomplete host-cell assessment, short follow-up, and little evidence on recurrence. Mechanics are considered separately as device biomechanics, interfacial transport, microbial contact cues, and host mechanobiology, which function through different mechanisms and levels of evidence, rather than as a unified cause of disease. The proposed framework links antimicrobial findings with surface integrity, host compatibility, regeneration and maintenance to identify gaps in translational evidence. Its generalizability and ability to predict clinical outcomes remain untested.

item.title: Discovery of Novel Decarboxylase Inhibitors via an In Silico – In Vitro Approach for Enhancing l -DOPA Therapy in Parkinson’s Disease
item.description:
Abstract
Parkinson’s disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disease, with increasing global prevalence. Its hallmark motor symptoms are managed most effectively with levodopa (l-DOPA), which remains the mainstay of symptomatic therapy. The oral bioavailability of l-DOPA is low and variable for several reasons, among which presystemic decarboxylation by human DOPA decarboxylase (DDC) and by gut bacterial tyrosine decarboxylase (TyrDC) is a major pharmacologically addressable contributor. Current DDC inhibitors (e.g., carbidopa) fail to block bacterial TyrDC, allowing l-DOPA to be lost in the gut. Here, we report the discovery of inhibitors targeting both human and bacterial decarboxylases using a combined in silico–in vitro workflow. Virtual screening of 1.6 million compounds against Enterococcus faecalis TyrDC yielded 505 candidates; primary biochemical screening identified 22 hits (>20% inhibition at 100 μM). Hit expansion via similarity search and synthesis of a 23-analog library produced compounds with improved potency belonging to four diverse scaffolds. Selected compounds inhibited recombinant E. faecalis TyrDC with micromolar potency (IC50 10–360 μM) and reduced l-DOPA conversion in E. faecalis whole-cell assays (up to 70% inhibition at 100 μM). Some of the compounds also displayed moderate potency toward human DDC (IC50 59–871 μM) and low cytotoxicity toward HeLa cells (CC50 > 100 μM for most). A moderate correlation (r = 0.59) between TyrDC and DDC inhibition suggests partially shared binding features, and molecular docking of the most potent dual inhibitor into the crystal structures of both enzymes provided additional insights into binding mode similarities and differences between the two enzymes. Notably, several compounds reduced l-DOPA conversion in whole-cell assays without measurably inhibiting recombinant TyrDC, indicating that whole-cell activity in this system is not fully explained by direct enzyme inhibition. These four scaffolds provide starting points for the development of TyrDC- and/or DDC-directed inhibitors.

item.title: An In-Line Dynamic Light Scattering-Based Exploratory Approach for Time-Resolved Nucleation and Particle Growth Kinetics in Solvent-Antisolvent Nanoprecipitation of Poorly Water-Soluble Drugs
item.description:
Abstract
A deep understanding of nucleation and growth mechanisms in solvent-antisolvent nanoprecipitation is critical to achieve nanoparticles with the desired properties. However, real-time monitoring remains challenging. This work aims to demonstrate the feasibility of dynamic light scattering (DLS) as an in-line process analytical technology (PAT) for the time-resolved monitoring and characterization of scattering changes associated with nucleation and particle growth during the solvent-antisolvent nanoprecipitation of active pharmaceutical ingredients. Dexamethasone serves as a poorly water-soluble model drug. Thermodynamic solubility and metastable zone width are determined experimentally. The in-line DLS assessment reveals a characteristic four-stage profile, consistent with prenucleation clustering in supersaturated solutions, the onset of detectable nanoscale entities associated with nucleation, a postnucleation growth-dominated stage, and late-stage aggregation. Controlled supersaturation is examined by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) simulations and milli-fluidic mixing in a 3D-printed Y-mixer for kinetic assessment. A Python algorithm enables automated extraction of DLS-derived induction times (tind) data. Noteworthily, this combined computational, milli-fluidic, and DLS-based approach minimizes user bias and enhances the detection of subtle nucleation variations under various hydrodynamic and nominal final relative supersaturation regimes. Overall, the findings presented here position in-line DLS as a powerful PAT approach for (nano)precipitation process understanding and optimization. This approach follows recent trends in automation and continuous flow preparation at early stages of nanoparticles development.
